feed.headline: UK and EU agree draft deal to scrap Brexit red tape over food exports
feed.ai: The food deal, ahead of a UK-EU summit later this month, is the most significant part of the so-called Brexit reset agreed so far.

feed.headline: Emotional reunions with loved ones for Oleshky evacuees
feed.ai: The BBC's Dan Johnson travelled to the northern Ukrainian border with Belarus after evacuated Oleshky residents arrived in buses and ambulances following a temporary ceasefire.

feed.headline: Shock of rail tragedy gives way to sorrow and outrage in politically divided Spain
feed.ai: The latest train crash will pile pressure on the government of Pedro Sánchez, one month before the general election.

feed.headline: Europe Today: Democrats win Senate in rebuke of Trump as Poland’s constitutional crisis drags on
feed.ai: A blue wave has swept the US in the midterm elections, with Democrats winning the Senate and heading for a big House majority as votes are still being counted on the West Coast. We bring live analysis from Philadelphia and Brussels, plus Poland’s crisis, Ukraine talks and the EU enlargement race.

feed.headline: South Korea and Turkey sign financing pact as Seoul seeks role in planned nuclear power plant
feed.ai: Turkey and South Korea are expanding nuclear, defence and trade ties. Their latest agreement explores funding for nuclear projects, while Ankara weighs potential partners for its planned Sinop plant.

feed.headline: EU rules on Artificial Intelligence devices will apply in NI
feed.ai: Some EU rules on Artificial Intelligence will apply in Northern Ireland, the UK government says.

feed.headline: Poland Beefs Up Security at Border With Russia
feed.ai: Prime Minister Donald Tusk said there had been “disturbing movement” in Kaliningrad, a Russian region just north of Poland.

feed.headline: Russia Senses Opportunity in Polish Political Turmoil
feed.ai: After its sometime allies were ousted in elections in Hungary and Serbia, Moscow has seized on Poland’s constitutional standoff in its effort to weaken Europe’s support for Ukraine.

feed.headline: Why Orban and Vucic Broke With Trump on Election Denial
feed.ai: Rejecting President Trump’s election denial playbook, nationalist leaders in Serbia and Hungary opted for an orderly retreat.

feed.headline: Putin Breaks Down His Isolation, With a Big Assist From Trump
feed.ai: Notching wins from Washington, the Russian leader is talking with foreign leaders and could return to diplomatic center stage with possible summit meetings.

feed.headline: Armenia sees 'totally new global role' for South Caucasus 'as a whole'
feed.ai: Armenia’s Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan told Euronews that peace and convergence in the South Caucasus, based on a carefully balanced pro-EU political vector, create a major opportunity for the region, with "democracy as a strategy" for Armenia.

feed.headline: Russian bombing kills 31 people at Ukraine aid centre, Kyiv says
feed.ai: Officials say at least nine 3,000kg aerial bombs hit a southern Ukrainian village in what the president calls an "utterly horrific" attack.
